title: Tesla Robotaxis appear to go fully unsupervised in Austin ahead of Cybercab launch
summary:
Over the past two weeks, all 170 Tesla Robotaxi rides in Austin monitored by the crowdsourced Robotaxi Tracker were unsupervised, the site’s creator, Ethan McKanna, told The Verge.
That’s a substantial change from earlier this summer, when Tesla’s unsupervised fleet appeared to be stagnating or even shrinking.
Robotaxi Tracker showed just 28 active unsupervised vehicles across six Texas and Florida markets as recently as last week.
The shift comes as Tesla prepares to launch the Cybercab, its purpose-built robotaxi, in Austin as soon as this month.
Even after the jump in unsupervised Robotaxis, Tesla remains far behind its biggest robotaxi competitor.

title: Riot is ending development on its League of Legends fighting game
summary:
Riot Games is already winding down work on 2XKO, the free-to-play League of Legends fighting game, less than a year after its initial launch.
“Even in these highlight moments, however, we saw no meaningful, sustained change in 2XKO’s trajectory; only a fraction of what it would take to trend toward sustainability,” Riot says.
Just this week, Bloomberg reported that Sony is stripping live service elements from its in-development multiplayer Horizon title.
Earlier this year, Remedy announced a final major update for FBC: Firebreak, its live service shooter set in the Control universe — though like Riot’s plan for 2XKO, Remedy has chosen to keep Firebreak online.
Even Fortnite isn’t immune to problems, as developer Epic Games laid off staff in March following a “downturn in Fortnite engagement.”

title: The Unlikely Place at the Center of China’s AI Boom
summary:
This vast, arid land has long been China’s capital of sheep farming and coal mining, but over the last few years, it has become the hottest place in the country to build an AI data center.
DeepSeek is reportedly building a massive AI data center in Ulanqab, as are ByteDance, Alibaba, and Xiaohongshu.
The Ulanqab data center boom signals that now they are finally starting to catch up.
The BooniesInner Mongolia has been a data center hot spot for at least a decade, long before the current AI boom.
Inner Mongolia is much closer to Beijing and other major metropolitan areas in China than any Western data center hub is.

title: LG’s new OLED breakthrough can boost display lifespans
summary:
LG Display has unveiled a new OLED manufacturing method that reportedly results in panels that are brighter, longer-lasting, more efficient, and theoretically can be almost any size.
This new technology is called FLiPP (FMM-Less innovative Pixel Patterning), which LG Display describes as a “dream next-generation OLED” patterning method that aims to eliminate some of the existing limitations in OLED panels.
Compared to FMM panels, LG Display says that FLiPP enables OLED panels to be 1.6 times brighter and last 2.4 times longer, and reduces power consumption by 13 percent.
FLiPP is also “free from panel size and resolution constraints,” according to LG Display, which means it can be used for virtually any panel requirements, including VR and AR displays.
LG Display says it will start by applying this technology to “IT applications,” such as tablets and monitors, before later expanding to cover products like ultra-large TVs and 1-inch wearable devices.

title: Octopus Charge puts 210,000 US chargers in one app, without Tesla, Ionna or Electrify America
summary:
Octopus Energy has launched Octopus Charge in the US, Canada and Mexico, aggregating more than 210,000 chargers from over 20 networks with no markup on energy prices.
Octopus Energy’s new Octopus Charge app covers the United States, Canada and Mexico, with one payment method for every network it supports.
Octopus Electroverse, the European original launched in 2020, reaches roughly 1.5 million chargers across more than 1,500 networks in over 40 countries.
General Motors aggregates networks inside its own brand apps, but only for General Motors vehicles, while Octopus Charge will work with any electric car.
The comparison is worth keeping in mind next time European charging gets criticised.

title: Tesla sunsets its Solar Roof tiles
summary:
Tesla has discontinued Solar Roof, its solar panels designed to look like regular roofing tiles, Electrek reports.
Sources “close to the program” told the publication that Tesla has informed its third-party installer network that Solar Roof is no longer available to order, and that only conventional solar panels will be supplied going forward.
The dedicated Solar Roof page (tesla.com/solarroof) that launched almost a decade ago now automatically redirects to Tesla’s solar panel page instead, and the “Solar Roof” option is no longer available under the navigation menu for Tesla Energy products.
Tesla first revealed the Solar Roof project back in 2016, but only achieved mass production in March 2020.
Electrek reports that Tesla has now concluded that Solar Roof is not financially viable for the company.

title: Muon Space raises $250m from backers including Google and Salesforce
summary:
Muon Space has raised $250m in a round backed by Google and Salesforce, according to their announcement.
It is the largest cheque yet written to a company whose best-known product is a constellation that watches for wildfires.
Muon builds and operates FireSat, the wildfire detection constellation developed with the Earth Fire Alliance and Google Research, and it deployed the first three operational satellites in that system in July.
It is the same problem OroraTech is attacking from Munich, and the German startup is further along in orbit than Muon is.
It says it now operates 19 thermal-imaging satellites, against FireSat’s four, and its cubesats are small enough that it launches a fraction of the mass Muon does.

title: Privacy advocates call on Maryland to investigate data brokers
summary:
Privacy advocates call on Maryland to investigate data brokerstoggle caption Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesMaryland has passed some of the strictest data privacy provisions in the country.
But privacy and civil rights advocates say commercial data brokers are violating state law by collecting and selling Marylanders' geolocation data, as well as selling information to federal immigration authorities.
Maryland lawmakers, however, have attempted to put restrictions on what data brokers can do with Maryland residents' data.
Data brokers are barred from selling or sharing Marylanders' location data unless law enforcement has gone through a legal process to obtain a subpoena or warrant.
Data brokers in Maryland cannot comply with an ICE subpoena to seek a Marylander's sensitive data; instead, ICE must present a warrant, Nojeim said.

title: Updated: Electric shock gloves already in use by police departments in Bellevue, Omaha
summary:
Last May, the Omaha Police Department submitted a request to the Omaha City Council to buy 40 pairs of the gloves for a little under $66,000.
In one case at a high school, the officer used a glove on a student for "noncompliance."
Road patrol officers check out the gloves before their shifts, and all school resource officers have a pair assigned to them.
Administering an electric shock with the gloves is considered a use of force.
Cvitanov, with the Omaha Police Department, said he considers the gloves to be a lesser use of force than physical force.

title: Browser De-Slop
summary:
Browser De-SlopModern browsers ship with an insane amount of bloatware.
You can point and click in the browser settings to disable most of it.
Or, you can de-slop the browser by force using a policy file.
Policy File LocationsTo get started, create a JSON file at the appropriate path for your distribution.
Here’s a few that I’m aware of:Distribution Browser Path FreeBSD Chromium /usr/local/etc/chromium/policies/managed/policies.json FreeBSD Firefox /usr/local/lib/firefox/distribution/policies.json Ubuntu Chrome /etc/opt/chrome/policies/managed/policies.json Ubuntu Chromium /etc/chromium-browser/policies/managed/policies.json Ubuntu Firefox /etc/firefox/policies/policies.json RedHat Chromium /etc/chromium/policies/managed/policies.json RedHat Firefox /etc/firefox/policies/policies.jsonAllegedly, these policies are also supported on Windows via Group Policy and MacOS using plist files.

title: Silicon Valley's Hottest Robotics Conference Actuate Had Few Robots
summary:
At a sold-out conference in San Francisco for people who build robots, the robots were surprisingly hard to find.
For much of the past two decades, robotics was a difficult sell in Silicon Valley.
Now it's one of tech's hottest bets, as investors look beyond software for the next wave of AI.
One panel, fittingly titled "The Data Wars," brought researchers from Nvidia, Physical Intelligence, and Generalist, among others, to debate what kinds of training data robots need and how to get it.
US manufacturers have welcomed protection from subsidized Chinese rivals, while startups and researchers say that losing access to inexpensive Chinese hardware could leave the country further behind.
